This writ petition has been filed for a direction to the 4th respondent not to disburse the amount to the fifth respondent in respect of the compensation arrived over the lands acquired vide notification in S.O.No.1333(E) dated 08.03.2019.
2.
It is the contention of the writ petitioner that he is the absolute owner and the fifth respondent has no right over the property.
Hence, seeks direction.

3. Counter is filed by the fourth respondent to the effect that as there is title dispute between the petitioner and the fifth respondent, the compensation is now kept by the fourth respondent and the matter has to be referred to the competent civil Court under Section 3H (4) for ascertaining the ownership and apportionment of compensation.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.
Section 3H (4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 reads as follows:

( 4 ) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

5. It is the contention of the fifth respondent that the suit filed by the petitioner for permanent injunction is already rejected by the Court and the petitioner has also filed for a suit for declaration,
which is pending before the Court.
6.

Considering the above provisions, this Court directs the fourth respondent to refer the matter to the competent civil Court as contemplated under Section 3H (4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order.
Thereafter, the parties shall agitate their rights and thereby establish their ownership over the properties in the civil Court.
